title: A Typewriter for the Clock
premise: In the winter of 1893, widowed lighthouse keeper Felix Eriksen has spent two decades guarding the coast and the secrets of his late wife Marta, whose family fled a crime they did not commit. When census taker Ada Lindqvist arrives asking questions that echo an old warrant, Felix realizes the state has finally traced the missing heirloom — a typewriter that holds the only written proof of who truly committed the arson that destroyed the Voss estate. As the great storms sever the island from the mainland, Felix must decide which of his three kin — his daughter Signe, his brother Anders, or his ward Ida — takes the last berth on the icebreaker before the river freezes, knowing whoever stays behind can carry the typewriter to safety or be taken with it. In the end, Felix gives up his own place, rows the typewriter across the breaking ice himself, and surrenders it to a young magistrate who chooses justice over law, clearing Marta's name at the cost of everything he kept silent for.
about_author: Freya Sterling is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing lighthouse logbooks and census ledgers from the Baltic coast. She writes historical fiction about ordinary people caught between paper records and the truths those records erase.

chapters.title: The Question Too Many
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. During the autumn census, Ada Lindqvist asks not just household names but whether anyone named Voss ever lodged at the light. Felix lies smoothly, but her pen pauses too long. Emotional beat: the old dread stirring after twenty quiet years.

chapters.title: What the Lamp Remembers
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. He climbs to trim the wick and remembers Marta's last winter, when she made him promise never to let 'the machine' leave the island. Emotional beat: grief braided with duty, establishing the typewriter's weight.

chapters.title: Signe's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Signe's POV. The keeper's daughter tallies coal and oil for winter and notices her father hiding a letter in the oil locker. She says nothing, practicing the family silence. Emotional beat: love expressed as learned discretion.

chapters.title: The Storms Begin
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The first great gale of the season batters the point; a fishing boat founders and Felix saves two men, one of whom mutters about a magistrate coming north. Emotional beat: the sea as both protector and herald.

chapters.title: Ada Returns
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Stranded by weather at the light, Ada studies Felix's household ledger and finds a name inked out twenty years ago: M. Voss. Emotional beat: professional curiosity hardening into personal resolve.

chapters.title: Anders's Debt
chapters.summary: Anders's POV. Felix's brother arrives from the mainland, owing money to men connected with the Voss heirs, and begs Felix to sell whatever Marta left. Emotional beat: shame wearing the mask of brotherhood.

chapters.title: Ida's Lessons
chapters.summary: Ida's POV. The orphaned ward practices letters on scraps, dreaming of the typewriter she has heard ticking in Felix's locked room like a second heart. Emotional beat: longing for a past she was never given.

chapters.title: The Locked Room
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. He opens the room at night, reads one page still in the carriage — a confession naming the true arsonist — and locks it away again. Emotional beat: terror that truth is a thing he now guards against his wife's memory.

chapters.title: Ice on the River
chapters.summary: Signe's POV. News comes that the river ferry will make one final crossing before the channel freezes; after that, no one leaves until spring thaw. Emotional beat: the clock starting, invisible and merciless.

chapters.title: The Magistrate's Warrant
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. A young magistrate, Halvard Rehn, arrives seeking the Voss heirloom under warrant; Ada, torn, hides what she knows about the Eriksens. Emotional beat: law and conscience beginning their long argument.

chapters.title: Brother's Bargain
chapters.summary: Anders's POV. Anders offers Rehn information about the typewriter in exchange for his debts being cleared, then drowns his guilt at the tavern. Emotional beat: betrayal as self-preservation.

chapters.title: The Berth Is Announced
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The icebreaker will take exactly three passengers from the island; Felix counts his household — four souls plus himself. Emotional beat: the blurb's terrible arithmetic made real.

chapters.title: Signe Claims Her Place
chapters.summary: Signe's POV. Signe declares she will go to the mainland conservatory as promised years ago; Felix cannot bring himself to tell her the berth may cost someone else everything. Emotional beat: hope sharpened into entitlement she doesn't know she carries.

chapters.title: Ida Overhears
chapters.summary: Ida's POV. Ida overhears Anders bargaining with Rehn and understands, dimly, that the ticking machine could hang someone or save them. Emotional beat: childhood ending mid-sentence.

chapters.title: Storm of the Century
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The greatest storm in living memory strikes; the lamp room glass shatters and Felix keeps the light burning bare-handed through the night. Emotional beat: endurance as penance and prayer.

chapters.title: Wreckage and Witnesses
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Among wreck debris Ada finds a Voss family Bible washed ashore, its pages naming Marta Eriksen née Voss. Emotional beat: the sea surrendering what men concealed.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Light
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Rehn confronts Felix with the Bible; Felix neither confirms nor denies, but Rehn sees the answer in his face. Emotional beat: two stubborn men circling the same fire.

chapters.title: Marta's Letters
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Marta's POV, twenty years earlier: her flight from the Voss estate, the typed confession she carried, her marriage as sanctuary. Emotional beat: love chosen over lineage.

chapters.title: Anders Takes the Ferry
chapters.summary: Anders's POV. Anders secretly boards the supply ferry to sell his information on the mainland, taking one of the three berths without asking. Emotional beat: cowardice dressed as opportunity.

chapters.title: Two Berths Left
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix learns Anders has gone, leaving two berths for three people — and the typewriter still needs to reach the magistrate or the truth dies with the season. Emotional beat: fury and relief tangled together.

chapters.title: Signe Learns the Name
chapters.summary: Signe's POV. Signe discovers her mother was a Voss and that her whole life has been built on an alias. Emotional beat: betrayal by silence, the book's central wound opened.

chapters.title: Daughter Against Father
chapters.summary: Felix and Signe, alternating. Signe demands the truth; Felix offers protection instead. She calls him a keeper of lamps and lies. Emotional beat: love against duty, weaponized within a family.

chapters.title: Ida's Choice
chapters.summary: Ida's POV. Ida offers to stay behind so Signe can go, believing herself least entitled to rescue. Emotional beat: heartbreaking self-erasure that shames Felix into clarity.

chapters.title: Rehn's Doubt
chapters.summary: Rehn's POV. Reviewing the old arson file, Rehn finds the convicted man's confession contradicts the physical evidence — and matches nothing except what a typewritten page might prove. Emotional beat: the law questioning itself.

chapters.title: The Ice Breaks Early
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. A warm front cracks the river ice ahead of schedule; the icebreaker's departure moves up two days. Emotional beat: time collapsing, decisions forced.

chapters.title: Night Row
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix rows the typewriter across the freezing strait by night to place it beyond Rehn's easy seizure, nearly dying in the floes. Emotional beat: a man choosing evidence over his own survival.

chapters.title: Ada's Decision
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada intercepts Felix ashore, reads the confession page by lamplight, and must choose between her commission and the man she has come to respect. Emotional beat: conscience outvoting office.

chapters.title: The Confession Read Aloud
chapters.summary: Rehn, Ada, Felix together. The page names Elias Voss himself as the arsonist, protected by the family's silence; the convicted man was a scapegoat. Emotional beat: twenty years of held breath released.

chapters.title: Berth for One
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. With one berth left, Felix puts Signe aboard without telling her, giving the ward's argument to Ida instead and keeping none for himself. Emotional beat: the choice made in the dark before dawn.

chapters.title: Signe Refuses
chapters.summary: Signe's POV. At the gangplank Signe steps back off the icebreaker and gives her berth to Ida, refusing to be saved by a lie again. Emotional beat: reconciliation through defiance.

chapters.title: Arrest at the Light
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Rehn, bound by warrant, arrests Felix for concealing evidence; the islanders watch from the shore as the lamp goes untended. Emotional beat: justice arriving as loss.

chapters.title: The Light Goes Dark
chapters.summary: Ida's POV. Ida and Signe climb to keep the lamp themselves, following the instructions Felix drilled into them for years. Emotional beat: inheritance passing not through blood but through teaching.

chapters.title: Trial on the Mainland
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. At the hearing, Ada testifies to the confession's authenticity; Rehn argues the original conviction was procured falsely. Emotional beat: the machinery of law bending toward justice.

chapters.title: Anders's Testimony
chapters.summary: Anders's POV. Confronted with ruin, Anders confirms the Voss family's cover-up, trading his last shred of standing for his brother's freedom. Emotional beat: redemption arriving too late to be clean.

chapters.title: Verdict
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The conviction of the innocent man is vacated; Felix is released with a reprimand; Marta's name is formally cleared. Emotional beat: victory that feels like exhaustion.

chapters.title: Spring Thaw
chapters.summary: Signe's POV. The river opens; the family returns to the island together, four souls and no more secrets between them. Emotional beat: tenderness rebuilt on truth rather than silence.

chapters.title: The Typewriter's New Page
chapters.summary: Ida's POV. Ida types the first fresh page in twenty years — her own name, her own story — while Felix watches. Emotional beat: inheritance transformed from burden to instrument.

chapters.title: Ada's Letter
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada writes to Felix declining a promotion south, admitting the island taught her what records cannot hold. Emotional beat: unspoken love given honest shape.

chapters.title: Last Berth
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix stands the night watch alone, finally at peace with which silences were worth keeping and which were not. Emotional beat: the keeper reconciled with what he kept.

chapters.title: A Typewriter for the Clock
chapters.summary: Full cast, closing scene. On the anniversary of the storms, the family winds the clock, lights the lamp, and Ida types the opening line of Marta's true history. Emotional beat: time, truth, and love set ticking in the same room.
